# EngineX

> Koa-compatible HTTP server for Bun

EngineX brings the familiar Koa API to Bun's blazing-fast HTTP server. It provides a Koa-compatible middleware pattern with an onion-model composition, a trie-based router for efficient path matching, and batteries-included middleware for CORS, logging, error handling, and body parsing. EngineX is a zero-dependency, pure TypeScript library designed as a near drop-in replacement for Koa on Bun.

## Links

- [Documentation](https://pegasusheavy.github.io/enginex/)
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/pegasusheavy/enginex)
- [npm Package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pegasusheavy/enginex)

## Key Features

- Built on Bun's native HTTP server for high performance
- Koa-compatible `ctx` object with request/response helpers
- Onion-model middleware composition with async/await
- Trie-based router with O(m) path matching, path parameters, wildcards, and route groups
- Built-in CORS middleware with configurable options
- Built-in request logger with timing
- Centralized error handler middleware
- Body parser for JSON, form, and text content types
- Zero external dependencies -- pure TypeScript, just Bun
- Easy migration path from Koa (minimal API differences)

## Installation

```bash
bun add @pegasusheavy/enginex
```

## Quick Start

```typescript
import { Application, Router, cors, logger } from "@pegasusheavy/enginex";

const app = new Application();
const router = new Router();

app.use(logger());
app.use(cors());

router.get("/", async (ctx) => {
  ctx.responseBody = { message: "Hello from EngineX!" };
});

router.get("/users/:id", async (ctx) => {
  ctx.responseBody = { userId: ctx.params.id };
});

app.use(router.routes());
app.listen(3000);
```
